rows.uncertainty: Abstract only. 'More than 50% improvement' is partial repigmentation, not complete coverage or colour match; the grading scale is not given. Only one efficacy time point, 2 months after the single treatment, far short of six months; no later efficacy visit appears in the abstract, although side effects were followed for up to 2 months after the assessments [about 4 months after treatment]. No control arm, so spontaneous change cannot be excluded. Erythema and postinflammatory hyperpigmentation in 'a few patients' resolved 'within 2 months after the assessments', so they were still present at the 2-month efficacy assessment and may have affected the improvement grading and satisfaction ratings [inferred from the timing]. Mostly facial lesions, while the authors note the extremities are the most frequently affected areas in IGH, so the sample may not represent typical IGH. Gender ratio printed as '7 : 33' without saying which sex is which. Mean age 57.5 ± 10.9 years. Lesion counts, lesion size, laser settings and Fitzpatrick types not in abstract. Patient-level result; how per-lesion outcomes were combined into a patient score is not stated. Denominators for 90% and 82.5% are not printed [both fit 40].
rows.citation: Shin J, Kim M, Park SH, Oh SH. The effect of fractional carbon dioxide lasers on idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis: a preliminary study. J Eur Acad Dermatol Venereol 2013;27(2):e243-e246 (Epub 2012 May 31)

quotes.quote: A total of 40 patients with IGH were enrolled.
The hypopigmented lesions were treated using a 10 600-nm carbon dioxide fractional laser (CO(2) FL).
Two months after a single treatment, physicians' clinical assessments were performed and the patients' overall satisfaction was evaluated.
Two months after a single treatment, physicians' clinical assessments were performed
Two months after treatment, objective assessments performed by two independent dermatologists indicated more than 50% improvement in 36 patients (90%), compared with baseline.
33 patients (82.5%) were very satisfied or satisfied with just one session of CO(2) FL treatment.
Although a few patients complained of long-standing erythema and postinflammatory hyperpigmentation, these problems spontaneously resolved within 2 months after the assessments.
Although a few patients complained of long-standing erythema and postinflammatory hyperpigmentation, these problems spontaneously resolved within 2 months after the assessments.
No other noticeable side effects were observed.
The face was the most commonly treated area, although the extremities are epidemiologically the most frequently affected areas.
The mean age of enrolled patients was 57.5 ± 10.9 years and the gender ratio was 7 : 33.
Yonsei University College of Medicine, Seoul, Korea
